items.stem: An app answers stock-count questions from an index that refreshes hourly. Users need the current count, and policy questions must stay on the index. Which change meets both constraints?
options: Refresh the index every five minutes, and keep the snapshot as the only source.
Enable the SSE transport on the connector, so stock values stream in.
Route stock questions to a read tool on the inventory server, and keep policy questions on the index.
Route stock questions and policy questions to a read tool on the inventory server.
items.rationale: A read tool returns the value as it stands at call time. Policy text changes less often, so it can stay in the index (Inference).
items.trap: A faster index refresh looks like the fix for stale counts, but the index still holds a snapshot (Inference).

items.stem: A query contains an error code, and users also ask about the same docs in plain words. A semantic index alone misses the exact code. The fix must find both the code and the paraphrased passages.
options: Use a semantic index only, and raise the number of candidates it returns.
Store the codes as binary embeddings, which keeps exact matches.
Run two semantic matchers with different models, and merge both lists.
Run keyword and semantic matchers, then merge both candidate lists.
items.rationale: A keyword matcher finds exact codes, and a semantic matcher finds paraphrases. The merged candidate list covers both query shapes (Inference).
items.trap: A larger candidate count from the semantic index looks like coverage, but a vector match can still miss the exact code (Inference).

items.stem: A chat app must answer with live order status from a remote server. The app must not run an MCP client in its code, and answers must not come from a stored snapshot. Which two changes meet both constraints?
options: Define the server in mcp_servers, and reference it from one MCP toolset.
Copy the order status into the index every hour, and search that copy.
Send the request with the MCP connector beta header.
Read order status through MCP resources, which the connector loads.
items.rationale: The connector calls the remote server's tools from the Messages API, so the app needs no MCP client. The beta header enables the connector.
items.trap: MCP resources look like a live feed, but the connector supports only tool calls from the MCP specification.
